_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-04 03:58:05Z)**_

You’re right: this goal should recommend a full-plan graph. Codex did not classify it as a single run.

What happened:

- Your default planner is `cli:codex`.
- Codex produced an 8-node graph with a nested subplan and `0.86` confidence.
- DeadReckon gives CLI planners only 30 seconds. Codex’s first token arrived after 38.8 seconds; completion took 71.7 seconds.
- The timeout is silently converted to `None` in [start.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/start.rs:562), causing the deterministic ladder to take over.
- That ladder measured `0 enumerated items, 3 clauses, 1 imperative verb`. It recognizes `build`, but not the coordinated verbs `has` and `introduces`, so its “strong decomposition” rule failed and dropped to `default-single` in [course.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/course.rs:703).

The [persisted preview](/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/runstate/flappy-forever-039b2660/preview/build-a-version-of-flappy-bird-that-runs-nativel-c2ff8df6.json:1) confirms `"source": "fallback"`. The later [Codex response](/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/2026/08/03/rollout-2026-08-03T23-50-21-019fcae4-d31d-79e0-bd6a-93bef87ee331.jsonl:15) confirms it wanted a substantial graph.

This also explains why it happens “often.” Your previous two Flappy Bird attempts show the same pattern:

- Codex proposed 4 nodes; completed in 51.2 seconds.
- Codex proposed 5 nodes; completed in 73.0 seconds.
- Both became fallback singles after 30 seconds.

The graph engine makes this more likely because it now asks Codex to author complete node goals, checks, dependencies, and subplans—not merely return a shape label. The old 30-second timeout remains.

There’s also a cleanup defect: these planner requests carry no cancellation token, so the timed-out Codex process can continue producing an answer after DeadReckon has moved on ([types.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs:148), [cli_common.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_common.rs:147)).

For now, choose “New full-plan pass” or use `--mode full-plan`. I would fix this at the classification layer by:

- making planner timeout/failure visible instead of calling the result “focused”;
- using a schema-constrained, lightweight Codex planner request;
- making the deadline realistic/configurable;
- cancelling the CLI process on timeout;
- improving the fallback’s coordinated-feature detection.

No code was changed.
